buckets.hint: Amounts in {cur}, nominal, per year; bucket balances apply before the month's spending. Net need = living expenses + housing (without amortization) + pillar 3a contributions + income tax − AHV − PK pension − earned income, from the planned values of the current year (for the 3-bucket strategy with guardrails: living expenses according to the guardrails, after floor and ceiling); one-off spending, acquisitions, purchases and special taxes do not count. Target for buckets 1 and 2 = years × net need. January refill: bucket 1 first from bucket 2, the rest from bucket 3, then bucket 2 from bucket 3; if the return criterion is not met, nothing is sold from bucket 3 and bucket 2 is not refilled. A surplus in bucket 1 or 2 goes to bucket 3. A: at the start of the withdrawal phase (first retirement), at a pension fund lump-sum withdrawal and at the restart after “all buckets empty”: wealth (the lump sum) goes to bucket 3 first, then as in January without the return criterion; the targets are reduced by the months of the year already passed, and the net need is extrapolated to 12 months from the months from the trigger onward. B: inflows go directly to their target and appear as the transfer “external → bucket 3” (one-off inflows, 3a, sale proceeds without a subsequent purchase, emergency sales), “external → reservation” (sale with a purchase in the following month) or “reservation → bucket 3” (surplus after the purchase); buckets 1 and 2 are not refilled. “Before” shows the balance before the inflow. C (look-ahead): if bucket 1 does not cover the month's spending and the return criterion is met, C1 applies: same procedure as the January refill, with the targets reduced by the months passed since January and the target of bucket 1 increased by the month's one-off spending, without the surplus transfer to bucket 3. If the criterion is not met, C2 applies: bucket 1 is refilled from bucket 2, then bucket 3, so that it covers the spending and afterwards still holds (min(reserve, months until January) − 1) months of need; bucket 2 is not refilled. The surplus transfer to bucket 3 only happens in the January refill. If all buckets are insufficient, a property is sold in an emergency sale; without a property, bucket 1 may become negative until wealth is positive again.

guardrails.hint: At the first person's retirement, the initial rate is applied to liquid wealth (without sale proceeds reserved for a purchase). Every January, the withdrawal is adjusted for inflation – except after a year of stock losses as long as the current rate is above the initial rate. If the current rate (withdrawal / wealth) exceeds the initial rate by the upper guardrail, the withdrawal is cut; if it is below the initial rate by the lower guardrail, it is raised. Withdrawal = living expenses + housing costs − income and pensions (before taxes).

withdrawal.endowmentHint: Withdrawal in January = (1 − weight) × previous year's withdrawal adjusted for inflation + weight × target rate × current wealth. At 100 % this equals the fixed rate; with a small weight, the withdrawal fluctuates little but follows wealth slowly.
withdrawal.fixedRateHint: Every January (and at retirement), the annual withdrawal is reset to this rate of liquid wealth. The withdrawal is living expenses + housing costs − income and pensions (before taxes): living expenses follow from it and track wealth; planned spending only applies until retirement. Wealth is thus never fully depleted – but spending fluctuates. A floor can limit this.
withdrawal.guardrailsHint: The guardrails determine living expenses, the buckets the investment. The bucket targets use the living expenses of the guardrails.

Every January, bucket 1 is brought to its target from bucket 2, and bucket 2 from stocks – but only if stocks reached at least the threshold in the previous year. Surpluses flow into stocks. If bucket 1 runs short in between, money is taken from bucket 2 and then from stocks. Before retirement, the cash rule from “Wealth & investment” applies.

withdrawal.vpwHint: Every January, the share of liquid wealth is withdrawn that, at the assumed real return, uses it up evenly by the planning age (annuity). The share rises with age; at the planning age, everything would be used up. Spending follows wealth and fluctuates accordingly. A floor limits this.

The total over all years stays the same.

yearTable.wealthHint: Wealth (liquid, real estate, pension assets, total) is the balance at year end. Total spending, withdrawal, total income and deviation from plan are monthly averages of the calendar year.{taxHint} Total spending = planned spending from the plan plus rent or mortgage interest and other housing costs plus contributions to pillar 3a. Withdrawal = what is taken from wealth (actual spending minus income, before taxes). Total income = income plus withdrawal. Deviation from plan = total income − total spending: at 0 everything goes as planned; with guardrails & co., a negative value shows how much the strategy cuts spending. Inflation per year = change in the price index in the calendar year (in the first year since the simulation start). Withdrawal rate = annual withdrawal / total wealth at the start of the year. The annual withdrawal is the sum of the year's monthly withdrawals (for incomplete years, the monthly average times 12); wealth at the start of the year is the value of the previous year, in the first year the balance at the simulation start; nominal values are always used. If the withdrawal is zero or negative, the cell stays empty; if wealth is zero or negative, “–” is shown. An asterisk (*) marks an incomplete year (first and last).

taxes.introLocation: Income, wealth and lump-sum tax from canton, municipality and church tax according to the tax data of the FTA, with the direct federal tax on income and lump sums.
taxes.estimateNoteLocation: The tax is an estimate with the standard deductions of the canton. The taxable income is earned income (net), pension fund pension and AHV minus the deductions from income: the proposal of the canton with the standard deductions of canton and federal tax for single persons or married couples without children: social deductions, insurance premiums and savings interest (in years with earned income in the variant with contributions to the 2nd and 3rd pillar) and the flat deduction for professional expenses on the earned income, or an own value; if desired, also the contributions to pillar 3a. For married couples (two persons, married), the tariffs and deductions for married couples apply. The direct federal tax on the income is added. Lump sums from the pension fund and pillar 3a are taxed by the rule of the canton with the multipliers of the income tax and one fifth of the federal tariff, without deductions; lump sums in the same year are added together, for unmarried couples per person. Not included, among others, unless in the own value: individual deductions, children, imputed rental value, debt interest; poll tax and future changes in the law. The results show taxes rounded to 100 francs. No tax advice.

deductions.hintLocation: Each row applies either the proposal of the canton (standard deductions from the tax data, recalculated if the canton, municipality or marital status changes) or an own value (kept with such changes). A row applies from its point in time until the next one. Mortgage interest is not deducted automatically.
deductions.hintOwn: With own tables there is no proposal of the canton; without an own value 0 applies. A row applies from its point in time until the next one. Mortgage interest is not deducted automatically.
deductions.ownHint: Own value: amount per year in prices of the simulation start (grows with “tariffs with inflation”), optionally plus a percentage of the income; it applies to canton and federal tax. Income is net (after AHV and PK contributions, like the net salary on the salary statement) including pensions. Pillar 3a is not included; it comes from the plan. A value from the assessment already includes it and would otherwise count twice (input help: “of which pillar 3a”). Home ownership (imputed rental value, mortgage interest, maintenance) belongs in the own value; from 2029 without imputed rental value and without the interest deduction for owner-occupied property, for example with a row “from 2029”.

ai.title: Connect to AI
ai.intro: An AI program can open, compute and change your plans with VivaPlan. To do so it starts the program vivaplan, which is installed with VivaPlan. VivaPlan sets up nothing itself: copy the setup line of your AI program and paste it there.
ai.path: The program is located here on this computer:
ai.claudeDesktop.mcpb: Easiest: download the package {file} from the download page of the version and open it with a double click. Claude Desktop then asks whether to install VivaPlan.
ai.claudeDesktop.steps: By hand: in Claude Desktop open the file {config} under Settings → Developer → Edit Config, paste the entry below and restart Claude Desktop. If the file already has entries under mcpServers, add only the part "vivaplan": {…}.
ai.claudeCode.steps: Run the line in the terminal. VivaPlan is then available in every new session of Claude Code.
ai.chatgpt.steps: The ChatGPT desktop app uses the MCP servers from the configuration of Codex. Paste the lines below into the file {config} (create it if it is missing) and restart the app.
ai.lmstudio.steps: In LM Studio click Install → Edit mcp.json in the Program area (the file {config}), paste the entry below and save. With a local model your data stays on this computer; small models use the tools less reliably, though.
ai.privacy: Privacy: what the AI reads from your plan goes to the provider with Claude and ChatGPT; with a local model in LM Studio it stays on this computer. VivaPlan itself sends nothing.
